none: Only a bare heading; no commentary text.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews challenged limited knowledge because the Torah contains God’s speech and rulings; Muhammad replied that the Torah is little of much.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أن سبب هذه الآية أن اليهود قالت يا محمد كيف عنينا بهذا القول وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the Jewish question the correct occasion and says the verse is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو القول الصحيح، والآية مدنية

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say Quraysh predicted Muhammad’s speech would run out and he would be cut off.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: سبب الآية أن قريشا قالت سيتم هذا الكلام لمحمد وينجسر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Quraysh remarked on how abundant Muhammad’s speech was.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: قالت قريش ما أكثر كلام محمد فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s words are intrinsically unlimited; finite trees and seas make the idea imaginable through the greatest abundance humans know.
rows.anchor: والغرض منها الإعلام بكثرة كلمات الله تعالى وهي في نفسها غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says the words would not be exhausted by the stated pens and seas; it does not imply that adding more would exhaust them.
rows.anchor: وليس تقتضي الآية أنها تنفد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali takes God’s words to mean what remains in the realm of decree, not what has come into existence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: المراد ب «الكلمات» والله أعلم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group understands God’s words as referring to all things known to Him.
rows.anchor: وذهبت فرقة إلى أن «الكلمات» هنا إشارة إلى المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya notes that this understanding tends toward Muʿtazilism because they regard divine speech as created.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ينحو إلى الاعتزال من حيث يرون في الكلام أنه مخلوق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى
rows.claim: These readers pronounce al-baḥr in the accusative, coordinating it with the noun of anna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده من السبعة وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى «والبحر» بالنصب عطفا على «ما»

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority read al-baḥr in the nominative as a subject, with the following clause as its predicate; Sibawayh estimates “its state is thus.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس و «البحر» بالرفع على أنه ابتداء

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians coordinate al-baḥr with anna, which occupies a nominative position as a subject.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين هو عطف على «أن» لأنها في موضع رفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority read yamudduhu from the verb madda.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «يمده» من مد

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan reads yamudduhu from amadda.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «يمده» من أمد

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says madda and amadda have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة هما بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says madda extends something from itself, while amadda supplies something external; the seven seas are separate from the present sea.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة مد الشيء بعضه بعضا وأمد الشيء ما ليس منه

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad reads al-baḥr madāduhu, using the verbal noun madād.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد «والبحر مداده» وهو مصدر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “and a sea that it replenishes.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «وبحر يمده»

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads “God’s speech” in the singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «ما نفد كلام الله»

words: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says creating and resurrecting everyone is as easy as one person, since it is all by “Be, and it is.”
rows.anchor: لأنه كله بكن فيكون قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash relates that Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abu al-Aswad, and Nabih and Munabbih sons of al-Hajjaj questioned gradual childhood growth versus resurrection all at once.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أن هذه الآية في أبي بن خلف وأبي الأسود ونبيه ومنبه ابني الحجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you could see” expresses wonder at the unbelievers’ condition; the omitted consequence is more terrible because listeners fill it with their utmost imagining.
rows.anchor: لو ترى تعجيب لمحمد وأمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are unbelievers, as shown by the threat of Hell; their certainty now indicates they lacked it in worldly life.
rows.anchor: والمجرمون هم الكافرون بدليل التوعد بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bowed heads express humiliation, despair, distress at punishment, and longing to return to earthly life.
rows.anchor: وتنكيس الرؤوس هو من الذل واليأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech has an omitted introduction: they are saying, “Our Lord.”
rows.anchor: وفي القول محذوف تقديره يقولون ربنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They now perceive what they were told in worldly life but denied; they seek return when it can no longer help.
rows.anchor: وقولهم أبصرنا وسمعنا أي ما كنا نخبر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could guide all people by grace leading to belief and creating faith in their souls; Ibn Atiyya identifies this as Sunni doctrine.
rows.anchor: لو شاء لهدى الناس أجمعين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say God would present a sign compelling people to believe.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين تعرض عليهم آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya identifies that view with some Muʿtazilites; their premise is that withholding possible faith-inducing grace would be unwise.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول بعض المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their argument is that anyone able to provide faith-inducing grace but unwilling to do so would act without wisdom.
rows.anchor: والذي يقود المعتزلة إلى هذه المقالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-jinna means the devils.
rows.anchor: لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taste” abbreviates that they are told to taste the punishment.
rows.anchor: وقوله فذوقوا بمعنى يقال لهم ذوقوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain nasītum as “you left.”
rows.anchor: ونسيتم معناه تركتم، قاله ابن عباس وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted noun is understood before “you forgot,” such as an action or promise.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف مضاف تقديره عمل أو عدة ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God names the punishment by the name of the sin: “We forgot you.”
rows.anchor: وقوله إنا نسيناكم سمى العقوبة باسم الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds are sins they earned.
rows.anchor: وقوله بما كنتم تعملون أي بتكسبكم الآثام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers prostrate when reminded of God’s signs, glorify Him, and avoid arrogance, unlike unbelievers who turn away and display pride.
rows.anchor: ثم أثنى عز وجل على القوم الذين يؤمنون بآياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is one of the obligatory prostrations in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وهذه السجدة من عزائم سجود القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prostration here means bowing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: السجود هنا بمعنى الركوع

rows.speaker: ابن جريج ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Mujahid report that the verse concerned hypocrites who left the mosque at prayer time; on that account it is Medinan and intends bowing.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن جريج ومجاهد أن هذه الآية نزلت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s practice was for a reciter at a prostration verse to bow; he supported it with David’s bowing and repentance.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فمن مذهب ابن عباس أن القارئ للسجدة يركع

none: Only a bare heading; no commentary text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “them” refers to Quraysh’s unbelievers.
rows.anchor: الضمير في قوله لنذيقنهم لكفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will make them suffer a worldly punishment short of the afterlife’s punishment.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله تعالى أنه يصيبهم بعذاب دون عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi and Muqatil identify it as the famine years God inflicted.
rows.anchor: فقال إبراهيم النخعي ومقاتل: هم السنون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and Ibn Zayd identify it as worldly afflictions such as illness.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب: هو مصائب الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Hasan ibn Ali say it is death by the sword, as at Badr and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والحسن بن علي هو القتل بالسيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the sword interpretation, returners are survivors different from those who tasted it, so the pronouns differ in reference.
rows.anchor: فيكون على هذا التأويل الراجع غير الذي يذوق

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb also identifies it with the striking, al-lizam, and smoke.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب أيضا هي البطشة، واللزام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says it refers to prescribed legal penalties.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا عنى بذلك الحدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legal-penalty view can apply to sinful believers.
rows.anchor: ويتجه على هذا التأويل أن تكون في فسقة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies it as punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عنى بذلك عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Who is more unjust?” expresses astonishment and means no one is more unjust than the person described.
rows.anchor: ومن أظلم على جهة التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who turns away contrasts with believers previously described as prostrating when reminded.
rows.anchor: وهي بخلاف ما تقدم في صفة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here criminals are those daring to commit disbelief and sins; the apparent referent is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وهم المتجاسرون على ركوب الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: يزيد بن رفيع
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports Yazid ibn Rafiʿ saying this threat applies to the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن يزيد بن رفيع

rows.speaker: يزيد بن رفيع
rows.claim: Yazid means those who say the matter is newly determined and human acts originate from the human agent.
rows.anchor: يزيد بن رفيع أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls this application plainly far-fetched.
rows.anchor: في هذا المنزع من البعد ما لا خفاء به

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muʿadh reports the Prophet saying that unjust banners, disobeying parents, and supporting an oppressor are offenses.
rows.anchor: وروى معاذ بن جبل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

none: Only a bare heading; no commentary text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adopted sons must be addressed by biological fathers; when fathers are unknown, they are brothers in religion and allies.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى في هذه الآية بدعاء الأدعياء إلى آبائهم

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: People cited Zayd ibn Haritha and Salim, client of Abu Hudhayfa, among those addressed through adoptive lineage.
rows.anchor: فقال الناس زيد بن حارثة وسالم مولى أبي حذيفة

rows.speaker: أبو بكرة
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says Abu Bakra recited the verse and said that, not knowing his father, he was the community’s brother and ally.
rows.anchor: أن أبا بكرة قرأ هذه الآية ثم قال

rows.speaker: الراوي
rows.claim: The narrator adds that Abu Bakra would have claimed his father even if he learned the man was a donkey.
rows.anchor: قال الراوي: ولو علم والله أن أباه حمارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqsaṭ means more just.
rows.anchor: وأقسط معناه أعدل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Prophet warned that anyone knowingly claiming another man as his father is forbidden Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بلغنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse removes blame for mistaken, forgotten, or habitual attribution, while deliberate attribution remains blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وليس عليكم جناح الآية رفع للحرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness concerns conduct before the prohibition; these attributes also apply generally.
rows.anchor: وكان الله غفورا رحيما يريد لما مضى

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group takes “their error” as earlier habit; Ibn Atiyya says this was not error before prohibition and here means forgetfulness or non-intent.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة «خطأهم» فيما كان سلف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada distinguishes sincerely believing someone is a man’s son from knowingly assigning him to a man other than his father.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن قتادة أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The penalty for mistake is lifted from this community.
rows.anchor: والخطأ مرفوع عن هذه الأمة عقابه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says mistake, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says he does not fear forgetfulness for his community, but fears deliberate wrongdoing; the quotation continues on the next page.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما أخشى عليكم النسيان. وإنما أخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse removes early Islamic rules, including refusal to pray over a debtor, and means believers must love and obey the Prophet above themselves.
rows.anchor: أزال الله تعالى بها أحكاما كانت في صدر الإسلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says wealth left by a believer goes to heirs, while debt or dependents become his responsibility.
rows.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين نزلت هذه الآية: «أنا أولى

rows.speaker: العلماء العارفين
rows.claim: Some learned authorities say the Prophet is more entitled because selves call people toward ruin while he calls to salvation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء العارفين هو أولى بهم من أنفسهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Prophet’s image of holding people back from the Fire while they rush like moths supports this view.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا قوله عليه السلام «أنا آخذ بحجزكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wives are mothers in marriage sanctity and honor; they were veiled unlike actual mothers.
rows.anchor: وشرف تعالى أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن جعلهن أمهات المؤمنين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Masruq reports that Aisha said she was mother only to the believers’ men when a woman called her mother.
rows.anchor: قال مسروق قالت امرأة لعائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex adds that the Prophet is a father to believers.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب «وأزواجه أمهاتهم وهو أب لهم»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads an addition identifying the Prophet as father, then says his wives are mothers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «من أنفسهم وهو أب لهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم»

rows.speaker: عمر وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Umar objected to Ibn Abbas’s reading; Ubayy confirmed it was in his codex and spoke sharply to Umar.
rows.anchor: وسمع عمر هذه القراءة فأنكرها

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Some interpret Lot’s “these are my daughters” as believing women whom men should marry.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في قول لوط عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood relatives became more entitled than earlier inheritance arrangements based on religious brotherhood and migration, which no longer have legal effect.
rows.anchor: ثم حكم بأن أولي الأرحام أحق مما كانت الشريعة قررته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the Book of God” can mean the Qur’an or Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: في كتاب الله يحتمل أن يريد القرآن

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن وعطاء وابن الحنفية
rows.claim: Qatada, al-Hasan, Ata, and Ibn al-Hanafiyya say the exception means kindness, maintaining ties, and a bequest at death.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تفعلوا يريد الإحسان في الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such acts are permissible toward an ally, including bequests to non-Muslim relatives.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله جائز أن يفعل مع الولي على أقسامه

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether a non-Muslim relative may be executor: some permit it, some forbid it, and some defer to the ruler, including Malik.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء هل يجعل هو وصيا

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد والرماني
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, al-Rummani, and others understand “your allies” as allies among believers.
rows.anchor: وذهب مجاهد وابن زيد والرماني وغيره إلى أن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Muhammad says the wording supports believer-allies, while general wali also works: kinship persists across religious difference, though Muslim-style affection does not.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الآية يعضد هذا المذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mastūr means written down; al-Ajjaj’s line about earlier scriptures illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: ومسطورا من قولك سطرت الكتاب إذا أثبته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada notes a variant reading, “that was written with God.”
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وفي بعض القراءة «كان ذلك عند الله مكتوبا»

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse honors the Messenger, states his rank before God, and clears him of suspicion concerning his wives.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية شرف الله بها رسوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group takes the pronoun in yuṣallūna as referring jointly to God and the angels.
rows.anchor: قالت فرقة الضمير فيه لله وللملائكة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group supplies an ellipsis: God blesses the Prophet and angels bless him, so the pronoun does not combine them.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: في الكلام حذف تقديره إن الله يصلي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A third group says joining God and angels in one pronoun is permissible; the preacher was criticized for pausing after “whoever disobeys them.”
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل جمع الله تعالى الملائكة مع نفسه في ضمير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Dawud’s version has the Prophet say “whoever disobeys them”; Muslim’s report tells the preacher to name God and His Messenger separately.
rows.anchor: ومما يؤيد هذا أن في كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مصنف أبي داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Prophet may have corrected the preacher’s pause then improved the whole wording; separating pronouns is preferable though joining is allowed.
rows.anchor: «بئس الخطيب أنت» لموضع) خطأه في الوقف

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority read the final tāʾ of malāʾikatahu in the accusative, coordinating it with the explicit noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وملائكته» بنصب التاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads malāʾikatuhu in the nominative, coordinating it with the syntactic position before inna; Ibn Atiyya questions this.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «وملائكته» رفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ṣalāt is mercy and blessing; angels’ is supplication; believers’ is supplication and reverence.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الله رحمة منه وبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending blessings at all times is an emphatic sunnah duty that should not be neglected.
rows.anchor: والصلاة على رسول الله في كل حين من الواجبات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urged frequent blessings on him on Friday, a witnessed day.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام: «أكثروا من الصلاة علي يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that companions asked how to send blessings; the Prophet taught a prayer invoking blessings on Muhammad’s family as on Abraham’s.
rows.anchor: من طريق ابن عباس أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The prayer asks for mercy and blessing on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham’s; reports vary in wording.
rows.anchor: وارحم محمدا وآل محمد كما رحمت وباركت على إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads faṣallū with an added fāʾ, strengthening the conditional sense: God blesses, so you bless.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «يا أيها الذين آمنوا فصلوا عليه»

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah adds “as God has blessed him” before the greeting command.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله «صلوا عليه كما صلى الله عليه وسلموا تسليما»

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say harming God means disbelief, attributing spouse, child, or partner to Him, or describing Him unfittingly.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور معناه بالكفر ونسبة الصاحبة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a divine report, God says a servant insults Him by claiming He has a child and denies resurrection.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث قال الله شتمني عبدي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says harming God means making images and trying to do what only God does by creating.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة معناه بالتصوير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet invoked God’s curse on image-makers.
rows.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لعن الله المصورين»

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group supplies an omitted noun, meaning “they harm God’s allies.”
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة ذلك على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about people attacking the Prophet when he married Safiyya bint Huyayy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت في الذين طعنوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Objecting to the Prophet’s appointment of Usama also counted as harming him.
rows.anchor: والطعن في تأمير أسامة إذاية له عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿn means exclusion from every good.
rows.anchor: ولعنوا معناه أبعدوا من كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harming believers includes vicious words and acts, false slander, and flagrant lies.
rows.anchor: وإذاية المؤمنين والمؤمنات هي أيضا بالأفعال

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Umar feared that beating and rebuking people made him one who harms believers; Ubayy said he was a teacher and reformer.
rows.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال يوما لأبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Abu Hatim says Umar recited the phrase, asked Ubayy how he read it, and Ubayy recited it as Umar had.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو حاتم أن عمر بن الخطاب قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about provision from heaven and earth is an argument; the Prophet is told to answer Allah because opponents are stunned.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى نبيه على جهة الاحتجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an obvious question, state the answer briefly and move to the next proof.
rows.anchor: وهذه السبيل في كل سؤال جوابه في غاية الوضوح

words: وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We or you” softens the invitation and prompts reflection, like telling an opponent one of you must be wrong; the addressees are implied to be astray.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وإنا أو إياكم تلطف في الدعوة والمحاورة

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of the two predicates is omitted because the remaining predicate signals it.
rows.anchor: وحذف أحد الخبرين لدلالة الباقي عليه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda takes aw as “and,” yielding “we and you are on guidance or error,” with two predicates.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أو في الآية بمعنى واو النسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects Abu Ubayda’s parsing as unsupported by the wording, though both analyses put guidance with believers and error with unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول غير متجه واللفظ لا يساعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that each side answers for its deeds is a truce and disengagement, abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: قل لا تسئلون عما أجرمنا الآية مهادنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the parties from their graves and opens judgment between them; al-Fattah means judge, a Yemen usage.
rows.anchor: وقوله يفتح معناه يحكم والفتاح القاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the truce and the statement about God judging between them are abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله منسوخ بآية السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correct reading of “show me” is inner sight, making “partners” a third object: prove how partnership could be.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى قل أروني يحتمل أن تكون رؤية قلب

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group takes “show me” as eyesight and “partners” as a circumstantial accusative referring to those made partners.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة هي رؤية بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the eyesight reading because looking with the eyes serves no purpose here.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأن استدعاء رؤية العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects associating partners with God, then describes Him with fitting attributes of might and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقوله كلا رد لما تقرر من مذهبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūliju means “makes enter”: night’s lost portion is added to day as if entering it, and vice versa.
rows.anchor: يولج معناه يدخل، وهذه عبارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the article in “sun and moon” as referring to the known celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في الشمس والقمر هي للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the article as extra, without reference or definiteness; Ibn Atiyya says this is sounder.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي زائدة لا معنى لها ولا تعريف وهذا أصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is identified as the coming of the Hour.
rows.anchor: و «الأجل المسمى» هو قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the term as the spans of night and day, making ajl a generic noun.
rows.anchor: وقيل آماد الليل وآماد النهار

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority read tadʿūhum with second-person tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «تدعون» بالتاء

rows.speaker: الحسن ويعقوب
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Yaʿqub read yadʿūna with third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويعقوب «يدعون» بالياء من تحت

rows.speaker: الحجة
rows.claim: The standard explanation of qitmir is the thin membrane over a date stone.
rows.anchor: و «القطمير» القشرة الرقيقة التي على نوى التمرة

rows.speaker: جوبير والضحاك
rows.claim: Jubayr through his authorities and al-Dahhak say qitmir is the cap atop a date; Ibn Atiyya prefers the membrane explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال جوبير عن رجاله «القطمير» القمع الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols’ nullity is first shown by their inability to hear prayer.
rows.anchor: أولها أنها لا تسمع إن دعيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if idols heard, they would not answer; this anticipates the contrived objection that they might hear.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنها لا تجيب أن لو سمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third sign is that idols disavow their worshippers on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: والثالث أنها تتبرأ يوم القيامة من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshippers’ shirk is attributed to idols because worshippers established them as partners; the verbal noun is attached to its agent.
rows.anchor: فأضاف الشرك إليهم من حيث هم قرروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is spoken disavowal, with God giving idols the cognition required to speak.
rows.anchor: وقوله يكفرون يحتمل أن يكون بكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, disavowal is figurative: idols remain inert while speakers move and argue; Dhu al-Rumma’s ruined-dwelling poem illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون بما يظهر هناك من جمودها

rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: Commentators including Qatada say the expert is God, whose truthful report guarantees the outcome.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون قتادة وغيره «الخبير» هنا أراد به تعالى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this continues the idols’ testimony: no informant is like one reporting about itself, and idols testify against their worshippers.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله ولا ينبئك مثل خبير من تمام ذكر الأصنام

none: Only a bare heading; no commentary text.
